notes.light.intensity: mapped to light.diffuse_scale with factor 1/0.7 — the compiled model's own light diffuse. RANGE GAP at the dark end: our scale is Box(0.2, 1.8), so the reachable intensity is [0.140, 1.0] (1.8 * 0.7 clips to 1.0 at the bright end, which costs nothing because swm's range stops at 1.0), and swm's [0, 0.140) is not reachable. swm's default 0.7 is reached at scale 1.000000.
notes.floor.color: Our ``floor.color`` is swm's leaf in shape, order, units and default: (2,3) rgb1/rgb2 of the builtin ``grid`` checker, with the default READ from dm_control's own common/materials.xml -- the same file swm's init_value [[.1,.2,.3],[.2,.3,.4]] transcribes -- so it is `identical`, not a rename or a scale. swm honours the leaf by rewriting the MJCF and RECOMPILING; we substitute the compiled texture's texels on the plate rig's own model and re-upload the texture to its own GL context, which needs no recompile and no second render context. VERIFIED byte-for-byte, not argued: over all twelve parity cells, three probe colours and eight states at 84 px, the substituted ``tex_data`` and the rendered frames are IDENTICAL to a full recompile of the suite at the same floor.color (tests/fixtures/regression/join/step8/capability/bake_vs_recompile_probe{0,1,2}.json). The suite's markrgb equals its rgb2, so the 1,196 edge-mark texels are separated positionally and left alone exactly as swm's recompile leaves them.

THE REASON CHANGED IN STEP 8 AND THE NEW ONE IS NARROWER. The skybox of the DELIVERED frame comes from the MuJoCo-baked plate, not from the mujoco_warp pass (the composite takes mujoco_warp only under the mover mask), so substituting the skybox texels on the plate rig and re-uploading moves 62.2-74.5 % of the frame with no second context -- and that IS the operation swm performs, which does not recompile either. What blocks the leaf is the DEFAULT, not the mechanism. swm FLATTENS the skybox to one colour, and this family's skybox is a 16-colour gradient (.44 .85 .56 to .46 .87 .58 over 6,144 texels), so no value of a flat-fill leaf reproduces our registered default appearance and no two-colour masked substitution reproduces swm's flat sky. Offering the leaf therefore moves this family's DEFAULT frame, which is a frozen pixel oracle on the frozen corpora. That is a re-freeze decision, not an implementation decision, and it is escalated rather than taken.

swm_only.goal.position: as goal.color. MEASURED: 0 px with show_goal=False, 2,648 px with it on

swm_only.floor.color: the checker floor texture's rgb1/rgb2. DEAD AT THE APPEARANCE WE REPRODUCE, MEASURED: it has an effect only when floor.pixel_encoding==0, and the official OGBench appearance is encoding 1 (the position-encoding gradient), where the recompile overwrites tex_data and the leaf moves 0 of 50,176 px. At encoding 0 it moves 21,029 px. Our floor.tint is a different knob -- a multiplier on whatever texture is bound -- not a checker rgb1/rgb2, so it is not offered as this leaf's counterpart
swm_only.floor.pixel_encoding: our `rendering.decolor_floor` is the same switch with the OPPOSITE sense: swm's encoding=1 is the position-encoding gradient, which is our decolor_floor=0, and both defaults are the official gradient. VariationMap can express `ours = theirs * factor` and nothing else, so an inverting relation (`ours = 1 - theirs`) has no representation here -- this is a capability gap in the shared class, reported to the workstream that owns it, not a renderer gap. UNSUPPORTED-PENDING-A, and pending a second measurement that the affine capability does NOT settle: swm's encoding=0 restores the XML CHECKER (2 colours) while our decolor_floor=1 paints flat slate. An affine `(factor, offset)` resolves whether the relation can be WRITTEN DOWN; it says nothing about whether the two settings draw the same picture, and that has not been measured. Mapping it on A's merge alone would invert the semantics for every caller and call a different floor the same floor
swm_only.light.intensity: the global directional light's diffuse term (MEASURED: writes light_diffuse row 0 only; intensity 0 moves 43,931 px, 0.5 moves 43,931 px at maxdiff 84, and 1.0 -- the default -- moves 0). Our renderer does not carry a light leaf: its lighting is a FITTED law with a fixed per-light split calibrated at the default intensity, so scaling the diffuse term is not obviously the same operation the official renderer performs. Offering it would need the law re-derived as a function of intensity and re-certified. ESCALATED
